idiom_name: JDK Proxy on the JVM, with scala.Dynamic/Selectable for member selection
implementation_notes: On the JVM Scala uses java.lang.reflect.Proxy and InvocationHandler for interface proxying exactly as Java does, and adds two language-level ways to synthesise member selection: scala.Dynamic (selectDynamic/applyDynamic/updateDynamic, which desugar arbitrary selections and need import scala.language.dynamics to define a subclass) and Scala 3's Selectable/reflectiveSelectable, which rewrites structural calls into applyDynamic backed by Java reflection; Scala 2 required scala.language.reflectiveCalls for the structural case. Both change what a call site can express rather than implementing a named interface at run time, so a real proxy still comes from the JDK.
pitfalls: Structural and dynamic dispatch is reflective: a wrong name or parameter class fails at run time with NoSuchMethodException, and the call costs far more than a virtual dispatch.
Selectable's applyDynamic needs the exact erased parameter classes unless the type mixes in Selectable.WithoutPreciseParameterTypes, so overloads that differ only by erasure cannot be selected.
updateDynamic belongs to Dynamic alone and has no Selectable equivalent, so an API built on assignment syntax is not portable across the two mechanisms.
